name: 45 Degree Hyperextension
description: A lower back exercise on a 45-degree hyperextension bench that targets the spinal erectors and posterior chain.
instructions: Set up on a 45-degree hyperextension bench with hips supported and ankles secured. Cross arms over the chest or place hands behind the head. Hinge at the hips, lower your torso toward the floor, then contract lower back and glutes to return to start.

name: 45-Degree Bicycle Twisting Crunch
description: A twisting ab exercise performed at a 45-degree angle to target the abdominals and obliques.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with knees bent and hands behind your head. Lift your shoulders and legs off the ground to a 45-degree angle and alternate bringing each knee in toward your chest while twisting the opposite elbow towards it, simulating a bicycle pedaling motion. Maintain controlled, twisting movement for each rep.
formCues: Keep lower back pressed to ground
Move legs in a controlled fashion

name: All Fours Groin Stretch
description: A floor stretch on hands and knees targeting the adductors and groin area.
instructions: Begin on your hands and knees. Widen your knees apart as far as comfortable, keeping your feet in line with your knees. Sink your hips back slightly until a stretch is felt in the inner thighs and groin, holding with steady breathing.

name: Band Assisted Pull-up
description: A vertical pulling exercise using a resistance band for assistance to build pull-up strength in the lats, biceps, and upper back.
instructions: Attach the band to a pull-up bar or sturdy anchor point. Step onto the band and grip the bar with your palms facing away from you, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Hang with your arms fully extended, keeping your core engaged and your shoulders down and back. Pull your body up towards the bar by squeezing your shoulder blades together and driving your elbows down towards your hips. Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Shrugging shoulders up toward the ears
Stopping short with the chin below the bar
Dropping quickly to the bottom without control

name: Band Bent-Over Rear Lateral Raise
description: A rear shoulder and upper back exercise using a resistance band in a bent-over position.
instructions: Stand on a resistance band, hinge forward at the hips with a flat back. Grip the band ends and raise your arms laterally to shoulder level, keeping elbows slightly bent, then lower with control.

name: Band Hip Abduction
description: A lateral leg movement with a resistance band to activate and strengthen the hip abductor muscles.
instructions: Place a resistance band around your lower thighs or ankles. Stand tall, shift your weight to one leg, and move the other leg out to the side against the band, then return under control. Repeat for both sides.

name: Band Hip Adduction
description: A resistance band exercise that strengthens the inner thigh muscles through hip adduction.
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a stable anchor and loop it around your ankle. Stand side-on to the anchor and bring your working leg across your body against the band’s resistance, focusing on squeezing your inner thigh.

name: Band Kneeling One Arm Pulldown
description: A kneeling single-arm band pulldown that trains the lats by pulling the elbow down from an overhead position.
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point above your head. Kneel down and hold the band with one hand, palm facing down. Extend your arm fully overhead, keeping your elbow slightly bent. Engage your lat muscles and pull the band down towards your side, bringing your elbow towards your ribcage. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
commonMistakes: Leaning the torso back to finish the pull
Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear
Bending and straightening the wrist during the pull
Letting the band snap the arm back overhead

name: Band One Arm Front Raise
description: Isolation shoulder exercise raising one arm forward against band resistance to target the anterior deltoid.
instructions: Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width apart and hold one handle with your working hand by your side. Keeping your arm straight but not locked, raise it in front of you to shoulder level. Pause, then slowly lower back down with control. Repeat on both sides.

name: Band One-Leg Kickback (Bent Position)
description: A glute-focused kickback performed from a bent-over position using a resistance band for added intensity.
instructions: Secure a resistance band around your working ankle and a sturdy anchor. Start on all fours with knees bent, kick one leg back against the band's resistance while keeping your core tight, then return and repeat for reps before switching sides.

name: Band Overhead Triceps Extension
description: A standing band triceps exercise where you extend your elbows overhead while keeping your upper arms mostly fixed.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band low behind you or hold it under your feet. Face away, grip the band with both hands and arms overhead, elbows bent. Extend your arms fully overhead while keeping elbows stationary, then return to the starting position with control.
commonMistakes: Elbows flare out to the sides
Lower back arches as the band goes overhead
Upper arms drift forward and backward
Only moving partway instead of fully extending

name: Band Prone Leg Curl
description: A hamstring isolation exercise performed lying face down and flexing the knee using resistance from a band.
instructions: Lie face down, anchor a resistance band at your feet, and loop the other end around your ankle. Curl your heel toward your glutes, contracting your hamstring, then slowly lower back to start and repeat.

name: Band Pull Through
description: A banded hip hinge that trains the glutes and hamstrings by pulling the band through the legs as you stand tall.
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at ground level. Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart. Step forward to create tension in the band, keeping your knees slightly bent. Hinge at the hips and push your glutes back, maintaining a slight bend in your knees. Lower your torso until it is parallel to the ground, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings. Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Squatting down instead of hinging back
Rounding the lower back as you fold forward
Letting the band pull the hips backward at lockout
Bending the knees too much and shifting into the quads

name: Band Resisted Decline Sit-Up
description: A decline sit-up performed with band resistance to increase tension on the abdominals.
instructions: Secure a resistance band behind your head or at chest level and lie on a decline bench. Perform a sit-up against the resistance, focusing on contracting your abs to lift your torso.

name: Band Seated Leg Extension
description: A seated exercise using a resistance band to isolate and strengthen the quadriceps.
instructions: Sit on a chair, anchor a resistance band behind you, and loop it around your ankle. Extend your knee to straighten your leg against the band's resistance, then lower back with control.
formCues: Do not lock knee at top
commonMistakes: Allowing the knee to drift or twist

name: Band Seated Row
description: Seated row using resistance bands that targets the mid-back and lats.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended, loop the band around your feet, and grasp the ends. Keeping your back straight and core tight, pull the band handles towards your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Slowly release to the starting position with control, maintaining slight tension in the band.
aliases: band one arm twisting seated row

name: Band Shoulder Warm-Up Stretch
description: A shoulder stretch and mobility drill using a resistance band to warm up the deltoids and rotator cuff.
instructions: Grip a resistance band with both hands wider than shoulder-width. Keep arms straight and move the band from hips, overhead, and behind the back to stretch the shoulders, then reverse the motion. Maintain a steady, controlled movement.

name: Band Side Bend
description: A standing lateral bend using a resistance band to target and strengthen the oblique muscles.
instructions: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding one end of a resistance band anchored at your side. Keep your torso straight and bend laterally away from the anchored band, contracting your obliques, then return to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Rotating the torso instead of bending laterally

name: Band Standing Calf Raise
description: Standing calf raise performed with a resistance band to strengthen the calves.
instructions: Stand upright with both feet on the band and hold the handles by your sides or shoulders. Press through the balls of your feet to rise onto your toes, stretching the band, and slowly lower back down. Maintain balance and perform the movement with controlled tempo.

name: Band Standing Crunch
description: A standing abdominal crunch using a resistance band to train the abs and obliques through spinal flexion.
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height. Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the band with both hands and bring it up to your chest, keeping your elbows bent and close to your body. Engage your abs and slowly crunch forward, bringing your chest towards your knees. Pause for a moment at the top of the crunch, then slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Pulling the band with the arms instead of curling the torso.
Hinging at the hips like a bow instead of rounding into a crunch.
Letting the band snap the torso back upright.
Standing too close to the anchor so the band has no tension.

name: Band Standing Leg Curl
description: A standing hamstring curl variation using resistance from a band for leg flexion.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at ankle height behind you, securing the loop around your ankle. Stand upright and curl your heel toward your glutes, keeping the upper leg stationary, then return to the starting position under control.
aliases: band one arm standing low row

name: Band Standing Lift
description: A diagonal band movement to train the obliques and core stabilizers.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band low to the side. Stand sideways and grasp the free end with both hands. With arms extended, lift and rotate your torso diagonally upward across your body, then return in control.

name: Band Standing Rear Delt Row
description: A bent-over band row with elbows flared out to target the rear delts and upper back.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the band under your feet. Hold the band handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended in front of you. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight. Pull the band towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Standing too upright and turning it into a regular row
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears at the top
Pulling the hands too low toward the waist
Rounding the upper or lower back while hinging

name: Band Straight-Back Seated Row
description: A banded rowing movement emphasizing the upper back and lats while seated with a straight torso.
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended, loop a resistance band around your feet, and hold the handles with both hands. Keeping your back straight and core engaged, pull the band towards your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then return to the starting position with control.
commonMistakes: Using momentum rather than back muscles
aliases: resistance band seated straight back row

name: Band Triceps Pushdown
description: An isolation triceps exercise using an overhead-anchored band to straighten the elbows against resistance.
instructions: Secure a resistance band to a high anchor. Stand facing the band, grasping it with both hands and elbows at your sides. Extend your arms downward, fully straightening the elbows, then return with control to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Upper arms swinging forward and back
Elbows flaring away from the torso
Leaning body weight onto the band
Stopping short of full elbow extension

name: Barbell Back Squat
description: Classic compound lower body lift with barbell across traps, targeting quads and glutes.
instructions: Stand with barbell placed across upper back, feet shoulder-width apart. Lower into a squat by hinging hips and bending knees until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Press through your heels to stand back up, keeping your chest up and back straight.

name: Barbell Bench Press
description: A flat bench press using a barbell to train the chest, triceps, and shoulders with a horizontal pressing motion.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended. Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in. Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest. Push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bar drifts toward the neck or stomach
Elbows flare straight out from the shoulders
Wrists bend backward under the bar
Hips lift off the bench during the press

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
description: A back exercise that rows a barbell to the torso from a bent-over position with an overhand grip.
instructions: Hold the bar with an overhand grip, hinge forward until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, and keep your back flat. Pull the bar to your lower ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower it under control.

name: Barbell Clean And Press
description: A full-body barbell lift that moves the bar from the floor to the shoulders, then presses it overhead.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and the barbell on the floor in front of you. Bend your knees and hinge at the hips to lower down and grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor, keeping it close to your body. As the barbell reaches your thighs, explosively extend your hips, shrug your shoulders, and pull the barbell up towards your chest. As the barbell reaches chest height, quickly drop under it and catch it at shoulder level, with your elbows pointing forward and your palms facing up. From the catch position, press the barbell overhead by extending your arms and pushing the barbell straight up. Lower the barbell back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Starting with the bar too far in front of the feet
Rounding the lower back when pulling from the floor
Catching the bar with elbows low and chest collapsed
Pressing the bar forward instead of overhead

name: Barbell Close Grip Bench Press
description: Bench press variation with close grip targeting triceps along with chest and shoulders.
instructions: Lie on a bench with feet flat, grip the barbell with hands about shoulder-width apart or slightly narrower. Lower the bar to your lower chest while keeping elbows tucked. Press the bar back up, focusing on extending through your triceps.

name: Barbell Curl
description: A standing biceps exercise where you curl a barbell from your thighs to shoulder height with an underhand grip.
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing forward. Keep your elbows close to your torso and exhale as you curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the bar until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps. Inhale as you slowly begin to lower the bar back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start the bar moving
Letting the elbows drift forward as the bar rises
Bending the wrists back instead of keeping them neutral
Dropping the bar quickly on the way down

name: Barbell Deadlift
description: A full-body pull that lifts a loaded barbell from the floor to a standing position.
instructions: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, feet hip-width apart. Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs. Brace, keep your back flat and push the floor away until you stand tall, then lower the bar under control.
formCues: Bar stays close to the legs
commonMistakes: Jerking the bar off the floor

name: Barbell Decline Bench Press
description: A decline barbell press done on a downward-angled bench to train the chest, triceps, and shoulders through a pressing pattern.
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Letting the wrists bend back under the bar
Pressing the bar toward the face instead of over the chest

name: Barbell Drag Curl
description: A barbell biceps curl variation where the bar stays close to the torso and the elbows move back as you lift.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up. Let the barbell hang at arm's length in front of your thighs. Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the barbell up towards your chest by contracting your biceps. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar swing forward away from the body
Bending the wrists back as the bar rises
Rocking the torso to start the curl
Flaring the elbows out to the sides

name: Barbell Front Raise
description: A shoulder isolation exercise where you lift a barbell straight in front of your body to train the front delts.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip. Keep your arms straight and lift the barbell forward and upward until it reaches shoulder level. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to start the lift.
Swinging the barbell with the hips.
Raising the barbell above shoulder height.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.

name: Barbell Front Squat
description: Squat variation with barbell held at the front rack position, targeting the quadriceps.
instructions: Stand upright, barbell resting across front shoulders, elbows high. Descend into a squat while keeping torso upright and elbows elevated. Push through your heels to return to standing, maintaining bar balance throughout.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: A glute exercise where the hips drive a barbell up with the upper back resting on a bench.
instructions: Sit with your upper back against a bench and the bar over your hips. Plant your feet, brace, and drive your hips up until your torso is level with your knees. Squeeze your glutes, then lower under control.
commonMistakes: Feet too far or too close

name: Barbell Incline Bench Press
description: A pressing exercise on an incline bench using a barbell to train the upper chest, shoulders, and triceps.
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle. Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Bouncing the bar off the chest
Lifting the feet or shifting on the bench
Lowering the bar to the neck or stomach

name: Barbell Lunge
description: A lower-body lunge with a barbell on your upper back that trains the glutes, quads, and hamstrings one leg at a time.
instructions: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell resting on your upper back. Take a step forward with your right foot, keeping your torso upright. Lower your body by bending your right knee until your thigh is parallel to the ground. Push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Repeat with your left leg, alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Taking such a short step that the front knee shoots far past the toes.
Leaning the torso forward as you lower.
Letting the front knee cave inward.
Pushing off the back foot instead of driving through the front foot.

name: Barbell Prone Incline Curl
description: A chest-supported biceps curl on an incline bench using a barbell to isolate elbow flexion with minimal body swing.
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle. Lie face down on the bench with your chest and stomach resting against it. Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms fully, allowing the barbell to hang down towards the floor. Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the barbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps. Inhale and slowly begin to lower the barbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench to help the bar up
Letting the elbows drift forward during the curl
Using body swing or kicking the legs to create momentum
Dropping the bar quickly instead of lowering it under control

name: Barbell Rear Delt Raise
description: A bent-over barbell raise that targets the rear delts by lifting the arms out to the sides while holding a barbell.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight. Raise the barbell out to the sides, keeping your arms straight, until they are parallel to the ground. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as you hinge forward
Swinging the torso to heave the bar upward
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Turning it into a row by bending the elbows too much

name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
description: A wrist flexion exercise performed with a pronated grip to target the forearm extensors.
instructions: Sit on a bench holding a barbell with an overhand grip, forearms resting on your thighs, and wrists hanging over the edge. Extend your wrists upward, lifting the bar, then lower under control.
commonMistakes: Letting the barbell roll in hands

name: Barbell Seated Behind-The-Neck Press
description: A shoulder press variation performed seated with a barbell lowered behind the neck to target the deltoids.
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support and grip the barbell with hands wider than shoulder-width. Lower the barbell slowly behind your head to just below ear level, then press upward until arms are fully extended. Use a spotter and maintain upright posture.

name: Barbell Shrug
description: A standing trap exercise where you hold a barbell at your thighs and lift your shoulders straight up and down.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell in front of you with an overhand grip. Keep your arms straight and your back straight throughout the exercise. Lift your shoulders up towards your ears as high as possible, squeezing your traps at the top. Hold for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to curl the bar upward.
Rolling the shoulders forward or backward at the top.
Leaning back and swinging the torso to move the bar.
Letting the head jut forward as the shoulders rise.

name: Barbell Skull Crusher
description: A triceps exercise that lowers a straight barbell toward the forehead while lying on a bench.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding the bar above your chest with a narrow grip. Keeping your upper arms still, bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, then extend your arms back to the start.

name: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
description: A standing forearm exercise where you hold a barbell behind your body and lift it by curling only your wrists.
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip. Rest the barbell on the back of your hands with your palms facing down and your fingers pointing towards your body. Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl your wrists upwards as far as possible. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause, then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the bar with the shoulders or torso
Bending the elbows to lift the bar
Letting the bar slip too far out of the hands

name: Barbell Straight Leg Deadlift
description: A barbell hip hinge that trains the hamstrings and glutes by lowering the bar down the legs with minimal knee bend.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing forward. Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Bend at your hips and lower the barbell towards the ground, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent. Lower the barbell until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. Engage your hamstrings and glutes to lift the barbell back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees into a squat as the bar lowers
Letting the bar drift forward away from the legs
Rounding the lower back near the bottom
Jerking the bar off the bottom instead of lifting smoothly

name: Barbell Underhand Bent-Over Row
description: Row performed bent over with barbell and an underhand (supinated) grip, targeting lats and biceps.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, grasp the barbell with a supinated (underhand) grip. Bend forward at the hips keeping your back flat, bar hanging from extended arms. Pull the bar towards your lower ribs, squeezing shoulder blades, then lower it until arms are straight.

name: Barbell Wide-Grip Upright Row
description: A compound barbell lift with a wide grip to target the shoulders and upper back.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a wide grip resting in front of your thighs. Pull the bar straight up toward your chest, lifting elbows high, then lower slowly.
formCues: Keep bar close to your body

name: Battling Ropes
description: A rope conditioning exercise using alternating arm waves to train the shoulders, forearms, and core.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Hold one end of the rope in each hand, with your palms facing each other. Raise your arms to shoulder height, keeping your elbows slightly bent. Begin making alternating waves with the ropes by rapidly raising and lowering each arm. Continue for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the whole torso instead of the arms
Letting the waves become uneven or stop
Lifting the shoulders up toward the ears

name: Bench Crunch
description: An abdominal crunch performed lying on a flat or decline bench to isolate the abs.
instructions: Lie back on a bench with your knees bent and feet on the bench or floor. Cross your arms over your chest or place hands lightly behind your head, engage your abs, and lift your shoulders off the bench before lowering them down under control.

name: Bench Dips
description: Bench dips are a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps by lowering and raising the body using a bench for support.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a stable bench and place your hands next to your hips, fingers forward. Slide your hips off the edge, keeping your legs extended, and lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, then press back up to the starting position.

name: Bench Pull-Up
description: A pull-up variation using a bench for foot support to reduce load and assist the movement.
instructions: Set a bench or box under a pull-up bar and place your feet on it for support. Grip the bar overhead and engage your lats to pull your chest up, using your legs to assist as needed, then lower yourself under control.
formCues: Don't let legs push too much

name: Bent Knee Lying Twist on Stability Ball
description: A rotational stretch on a stability ball that targets the obliques and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie on your back with your calves resting on a stability ball, arms extended to sides. With knees bent, gently rotate your knees side to side, engaging your core to control the movement.
aliases: Bent knee Lying  twist (On Stability Ball)

name: Bridge Pose (Setu Bandhasana)
description: Bridge Pose is a yoga stretch that lifts the hips to activate the glutes and open the chest and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and arms at your sides. Press through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling, engaging the glutes and lower back, and hold at the top for a stretch. Lower slowly to the ground and repeat as needed.

name: Burpee
description: A full-body bodyweight movement that combines a squat, plank, push-up, and jump for conditioning.
instructions: Start in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart. Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and placing your hands on the floor in front of you. Kick your feet back into a push-up position. Perform a push-up, keeping your body in a straight line. Jump your feet back into the squat position. Jump up explosively, reaching your arms overhead. Land softly and immediately lower back into a squat position to begin the next repetition.
commonMistakes: Hips sagging low in the plank or push-up.
Feet landing too narrow under the body.
Hands placed far in front of the shoulders.
Landing stiff-legged with no knee bend.

name: Butterfly Yoga Pose
description: A seated stretch that opens the hips and groin by bringing the feet together and letting the knees fall outward.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your back straight, bring the soles of your feet together, and allow your knees to drop out to the sides. Hold your feet with your hands and gently press knees toward the ground for a deeper stretch.

name: Cable Close Grip Lat Pulldown
description: A cable exercise using a close grip to target the latissimus dorsi and supporting back muscles.
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with a close (V-bar) handle attached. Grasp the handles with palms facing in, keep your torso upright, and pull the handle down to your chest by squeezing your back and bringing elbows down and back, then return the handle under control.
aliases: Cable Close Grip Front Lat Pulldown

name: Cable Crossover Reverse Fly
description: A cable rear-delt fly where you pull crossed low handles out and back to train the back of the shoulders and upper back.
instructions: Attach a D-handle to each low pulley cable and stand in the middle of the cable crossover machine. Grasp the handles with a pronated grip (palms facing down) and take a step forward, positioning your feet shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees slightly and lean forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your abs engaged. With your arms extended out to the sides and slightly bent at the elbows, exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the cables back and upward in a reverse fly motion. Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Standing fully upright and turning it into a row
Bending and straightening the elbows during the rep
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Swinging the torso to move the handles

name: Cable Kneeling Crunch
description: A kneeling cable ab exercise where you curl your torso downward against a high pulley to train the abs and obliques.
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a high pulley and kneel down facing away from the machine. Hold the rope handle with both hands and place it behind your head, keeping your elbows out to the sides. Keeping your hips stationary, flex your waist and crunch your torso down towards your thighs. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Pulling the rope down with the arms instead of curling the torso
Sitting hips back and turning it into a hip hinge
Jerking up and letting the weight stack drop between reps
Lifting the chest too high and losing abdominal tension at the top

name: Cable Lateral Raise
description: A single-arm cable shoulder isolation exercise that raises the arm out to the side to target the lateral delts.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip. Keep your arms straight and your core engaged. Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear
Swinging the torso to lift the handle
Turning the raise into a front lift
Lifting the hand far above shoulder height

name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension
description: A lying cable triceps exercise where you bend and straighten the elbows to move a rope handle over your chest.
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a low pulley cable machine. Lie down on a flat bench facing up, with your head towards the cable machine. Grasp the rope handle with both hands, palms facing each other, and extend your arms straight up over your chest. Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the rope handle towards your forehead by bending your elbows. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then extend your arms back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare wide to the sides
Drifting the upper arms backward and turning it into a pullover
Lowering the rope behind the head instead of toward the forehead
Bouncing out of the bottom instead of controlling the cable
aliases: triceps extension on bench with cable

name: Cable One Arm Curl
description: A single-arm cable biceps exercise where you curl a handle upward while keeping your elbow tucked at your side.
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp the cable handle with an underhand grip, palm facing up. Keep your elbow close to your side and slowly curl your forearm up towards your shoulder. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearm back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Elbow swings forward during the curl
Shoulder shrugs up toward the ear
Torso leans back to move the weight
Handle drops quickly on the way down

name: Cable One Arm Front Raise
description: An isolation exercise that raises the arm forward using a cable to target the front deltoid.
instructions: Stand facing away from a low cable, grasping the handle with one hand. Keeping your arm straight, raise it in front of you up to shoulder height, pause, then lower under control.

name: Cable One Arm Lateral Pulldown
description: A vertical pulling exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi using a single cable handle.
instructions: Sit or stand at a cable station, grasp the single handle with one hand overhead. Pull the handle down to shoulder level, pausing briefly, then control the return.

name: Cable One Arm Lateral Raise
description: A single-arm shoulder isolation exercise using a cable to lift the arm out to the side and target the lateral delts.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the cable machine. Hold the cable handle with one hand, palm facing down, and stand far enough away from the machine so that there is tension on the cable. Keep your arm straight and slowly raise it out to the side until it is parallel to the ground. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the working shoulder toward the ear
Swinging the torso to start the rep
Turning the raise into a front raise
Lifting the hand far above shoulder height

name: Cable One-Arm Twisting Seated Row
description: A unilateral cable row variation adding torso rotation to activate both the lats and core.
instructions: Sit at a cable row station and grasp the handle with one hand. As you row the handle towards your torso, rotate your upper body toward the working side, then reverse the rotation as you extend your arm forward.
aliases: one-arm seated cable row with twist
Cable One Arm Twisting Seated Row

name: Cable Pulldown
description: A seated cable back exercise where you pull a bar from overhead to your upper chest to train the lats and upper arms.
instructions: Adjust the cable pulldown machine so that the seat is at a comfortable height and the knee pad is secured. Sit on the seat with your back straight and your feet flat on the ground. Grasp the cable bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Lean back slightly and engage your core. Pull the cable bar down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the bar back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Pulling the bar behind the neck
Swinging the torso backward to start the rep
Letting the shoulders shrug up at the top
Stopping short and not fully straightening the arms

name: Cable Rear Delt Row (with rope)
description: A cable rowing variation with a rope that targets the rear delts by pulling the elbows out and back.
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a low pulley cable machine. Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp the rope handle with an overhand grip, palms facing each other. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight. Keep your elbows slightly bent and pull the rope towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Standing fully upright and turning it into a regular cable row
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears during the pull
Pulling mostly with the hands and curling the rope in
Rounding the upper back as the rope returns forward

name: Cable Rope Overhead Triceps Extension
description: An isolation exercise using a rope attachment on a high pulley to target the triceps overhead.
instructions: Stand or kneel with your back to the high pulley, grasping the rope with both hands. Lean forward slightly, extend your elbows to press the rope forward/upward, then return to start under control.
aliases: Cable Rope High Pulley Overhead Triceps Extension

name: Cable Rope Triceps Pushdown
description: A cable isolation exercise targeting the triceps by pressing a rope attachment downward.
instructions: Stand facing a cable stack with a rope attached to the high pulley. Grasp the rope with both hands, elbows at your sides, and push the rope downward by extending your arms. Control the movement back to the starting position for each rep.
formCues: Split the rope at the bottom

name: Cable Seated High Row (V-bar)
description: A seated cable row using a V-bar handle, pulling toward the upper torso to train the lats, upper back, and biceps.
instructions: Sit on the cable machine with your feet flat on the floor and your knees slightly bent. Grasp the v-bar attachment with an overhand grip, palms facing each other, and your hands shoulder-width apart. Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward from the hips. Pull the v-bar towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blades and squeezing your back muscles. Pause for a moment at the peak of the contraction, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as the handle moves forward
Leaning far back and using body swing to pull
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Pulling with the arms only and not moving the shoulder blades
aliases: cable high row with V handle

name: Cable Standing Crunch
description: A standing cable ab exercise where you curl your torso downward against a high pulley to train the abs and obliques.
instructions: Attach a cable handle to a high pulley and stand facing away from the machine. Hold the handle with both hands and place it behind your head, keeping your elbows bent. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent. Keeping your abs engaged, exhale and crunch your torso down towards your knees, bringing your elbows towards your thighs. Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Hinging forward at the hips instead of curling the spine
Pulling the attachment down with the arms
Standing too upright and barely moving the torso
Letting the weight yank the torso back up

name: Cable Standing Fly
description: A cable isolation exercise for the chest, performed standing and moving arms in a hugging motion.
instructions: Stand between two cable stacks, grab the D-handles, and take a step forward. With a slight bend in elbows, bring the handles together in front of the chest, then slowly return to the starting position.

name: Cable Standing Inner Curl
description: A single-arm cable biceps curl done standing with an underhand grip to train elbow flexion under constant tension.
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp the cable handle with an underhand grip, palms facing up. Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary. Exhale and curl the cable handle towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps. Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps. Inhale and slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Elbow drifts forward during the curl
Torso rocks back to move the weight
Wrist bends excessively instead of staying neutral
Letting the handle drop quickly on the way down

name: Cable Standing Lift
description: A standing cable core exercise that lifts the handle diagonally across the body to train the abs and obliques.
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the cable handle with both hands and position it at waist height. Engage your core and maintain a straight back throughout the exercise. Keeping your arms straight, exhale and lift the cable handle up towards your opposite shoulder, rotating your torso. Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows and turning it into an arm pull
Twisting the knees inward instead of rotating the torso
Leaning back or arching the lower back at the top
Letting the weight snap back down without control

name: Cable Standing One Arm Triceps Extension
description: A single-arm cable triceps isolation exercise done standing, extending the elbow while keeping the upper arm fixed.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the cable machine. Hold the cable handle with your right hand, palm facing down, and position your arm so that it is fully extended and parallel to the ground. Keep your elbow stationary and close to your body. Slowly bend your elbow, lowering the cable handle towards the back of your head. Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then extend your arm back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and perform the exercise with your left arm.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbow drift up and down during the rep
Turning the torso to help move the handle
Dropping the upper arm instead of keeping it level
Using momentum and snapping the cable back

name: Cable Straight Arm Pulldown
description: A cable lat exercise where you pull a straight bar from shoulder height down to your thighs with mostly straight arms.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the high pulley of a cable machine. Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, keeping your arms straight and your palms facing down. Engage your lats and pull the bar down towards your thighs, keeping your arms straight throughout the movement. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return the bar to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows and turning it into a triceps pressdown
Leaning back and using body swing to move the bar
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Letting the bar drift away from the body at the bottom

name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
description: An isolation cable exercise targeting the triceps by extending the arm downward against resistance.
instructions: Stand at a cable station with a rope or bar attached to a high pulley. Grasp the attachment with both hands, elbows at your sides, and push it downward, fully extending your arms before returning.

name: Cable Twist (up-down)
description: A standing cable rotation that trains the obliques by twisting the torso diagonally across the body.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the cable machine. Hold the cable handle with both hands in front of your chest, keeping your arms slightly bent. Engage your core and slowly rotate your torso to one side, keeping your hips and legs stable. Pause for a moment at the end of the rotation, then slowly return to the starting position. Repeat the rotation to the opposite side. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Turning the hips and feet with the cable
Bending and straightening the elbows to move the weight
Letting the cable yank the torso back
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears

name: Calf Stretch with Rope
description: A static stretch for the calf muscles using a rope or strap to pull the foot into dorsiflexion.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended. Loop a rope or band around your foot, keep your knee straight, and gently pull your toes toward you to stretch your calf.

name: Calf Stretch with Strap
description: A seated stretch using a strap or resistance band to elongate the calf muscles.
instructions: Sit on the floor with one leg extended and loop a strap around the ball of your foot. Gently pull the strap towards you while keeping your knee straight, feeling a stretch along the back of your lower leg.
aliases: standing hamstring and calf stretch with strap

name: Cambered Bar Lying Row
description: A chest-supported barbell row performed lying face down on a bench to train the upper back with minimal body English.
instructions: Set up a barbell on the floor and lie face down on a bench with your chest just off the edge. Reach down and grab the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. With your legs straight and feet on the ground, lift the barbell off the floor by extending your arms. Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Lower the barbell back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench to move the bar
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Yanking the bar off the floor with momentum
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides

name: Chest Dips
description: A compound bodyweight exercise performed on parallel bars to target the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
instructions: Grasp parallel bars and lift yourself to starting position with arms locked. Lean the torso slightly forward and lower your body by bending the elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor. Push yourself back to the start, emphasizing the chest contraction.

name: Chest Lift with Rotation
description: An abdominal exercise that combines a chest lift with torso rotation to target the obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Engage your core, lift your chest off the mat while simultaneously rotating your torso to one side, then return to start. Alternate rotations with each rep.

name: Chin-to-Chest Stretch
description: A gentle static stretch to release tension in the neck flexors by tilting the chin toward the chest.
instructions: Sit or stand upright. Slowly lower your chin towards your chest until you feel a gentle stretch along the back of your neck, holding the position for 15-30 seconds before releasing.

name: Chin-ups (narrow parallel grip)
description: A bodyweight vertical pull using a narrow parallel grip to train the upper back, biceps, and forearms.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a narrow parallel grip, palms facing towards you. Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body. Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears while pulling.
Swinging the legs or kipping to get upward.
Stopping short with the chin below the hands.
Dropping quickly to the bottom without control.

name: Close Feet Leg Press
description: A leg press using a narrow foot placement to emphasize the quadriceps.
instructions: Sit in a leg press machine and place your feet hip-width or closer at the center of the platform. Press the platform away by extending your knees while keeping your back flat, then lower under control.
formCues: Keep back and hips against pad

name: Close Grip Chin-Up
description: A vertical pulling exercise emphasizing the lats and biceps using a supinated close grip.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width or closer using a supinated (underhand) grip. Pull your chin over the bar by driving your elbows down and back, then lower under control.
aliases: weighted close grip chin-up on dip cage

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
description: A push-up variation with hands close together to emphasize triceps involvement.
instructions: Assume a plank position with hands placed close together under your chest. Lower your body, keeping elbows near your sides, and push back up to the top position.

name: Commando Pull-Up
description: A challenging pull-up variation using a parallel grip over the bar, emphasizing back, biceps, and grip strength.
instructions: Grasp a pull-up bar with hands facing each other and step sideways under the bar so your head faces parallel along the bar. Pull your chest toward one side of the bar, passing your head to one side, then lower and repeat on the opposite side. Maintain strict control and avoid swinging.

name: Crossover Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
description: A kneeling stretch targeting hip flexors with the trunk rotated across the body.
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with your back knee on the ground and front foot forward. Gently shift your hips forward and rotate your torso away from the back leg to deepen the stretch. Hold the position and switch sides.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
description: A chest pressing exercise performed on a 45-degree decline bench using dumbbells.
instructions: Secure your feet in the decline bench and lie back holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level. Press the weights up until arms are extended, then lower them until elbows are at about 90 degrees.

name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
description: A fly movement on a 45-degree decline bench to isolate the lower chest with dumbbells.
instructions: Lay back on a 45-degree decline bench holding a dumbbell in each hand above chest. Lower the weights in an arc to sides until a stretch is felt, then bring them back together, squeezing the chest.

name: Deep Push-Up
description: A push-up performed with hands elevated for a greater range of motion to emphasize lower chest activation.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with hands on raised platforms or handles to allow your chest to go deeper than standard push-ups. Lower your chest below hand level, then press back up powerfully to full arm extension.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
description: A bent-over calf raise on a step that trains the calves through a full heel drop and strong lift.
instructions: Stand with your toes on an elevated surface, such as a step or block. Place your hands on a stable support, such as a wall or railing, for balance. Raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bouncing at the bottom instead of lowering under control
Rolling the ankles inward or outward
Using the hands to push the body up
Cutting the range short and not dropping the heels

name: Dumbbell Alternating Shoulder Press
description: A shoulder press using dumbbells, pressing one arm at a time to target the deltoids and stabilizers.
instructions: Sit or stand with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. Press one dumbbell overhead while keeping the other stationary, then alternate arms for each repetition.

name: Dumbbell Arnold Press
description: A seated dumbbell shoulder press that rotates from palms-in at the bottom to palms-forward overhead.
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing your body and elbows bent. Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended and your palms are facing forward. Rotate your wrists as you lift, so that your palms are facing forward at the top of the movement. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back as the dumbbells go overhead
Letting the elbows flare straight out at the bottom
Pressing the dumbbells up without rotating the hands
Lowering the dumbbells too fast and losing control

name: Dumbbell Behind-the-Back Wrist Curl
description: A forearm isolation exercise curling a dumbbell behind the back to emphasize forearm flexors.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell behind your back with your palm facing back. Curl the dumbbell by flexing your wrist, then return to the starting position under control.

name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
description: A rowing movement that targets the back muscles while bracing the core in a bent-over position.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with feet shoulder-width apart, hinge at the hips while keeping your back flat. Row the weights to your sides by pulling elbows back, then lower the weights slowly.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
description: A standing arm exercise where you curl dumbbells from your sides to your shoulders to train the biceps.
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward and arms fully extended. Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps. Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start the curl
Letting the elbows drift forward as the weights rise
Using partial range and not lowering fully
Bending the wrists back instead of keeping them neutral

name: Dumbbell Close-Grip Press
description: A pressing movement with dumbbells held close together to emphasize triceps activation.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding dumbbells together above your chest, palms facing each other. Lower the weights while keeping elbows close to your sides, then press back up by extending the arms.

name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
description: A seated single-arm biceps curl with the upper arm braced against the inner thigh to isolate the biceps.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs spread apart and a dumbbell in one hand, resting your elbow on the inside of your thigh. Fully extend your arm and hold the dumbbell with an underhand grip. Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the weight up towards your shoulder while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps. Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
commonMistakes: Lifting the elbow off the thigh during the curl
Swinging the torso to help raise the dumbbell
Cutting the rep short and not fully lowering
Bending the wrist back instead of keeping it neutral

name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl
description: A dumbbell curl variation where each hand travels across the body to the opposite shoulder with a neutral grip.
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body. Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary. Exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps, bringing the dumbbells across your body towards your opposite shoulder. Continue to raise the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps. Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso or leaning back to lift the dumbbell
Letting the elbow drift forward away from the ribs
Twisting the wrist so the palm turns up at the top
Dropping the dumbbell quickly instead of lowering with control

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
description: A hip-hinge lift with two dumbbells that trains the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back while lifting from standing to lockout.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body, arms extended downwards. Bend at your hips and knees, lowering the dumbbells towards the ground while keeping your back straight. Push through your heels and extend your hips and knees, lifting the dumbbells back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as the dumbbells lower
Letting the dumbbells drift far in front of the legs
Squatting straight down instead of hinging the hips back
Locking the knees rigid or overbending them

name: Dumbbell Fly
description: A lying chest isolation exercise where you open the arms wide with dumbbells, then bring them together in an arc over the chest.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Extend your arms straight up over your chest, with a slight bend in your elbows. Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest. Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement and bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows like a press
Lowering the dumbbells too far below chest level
Bringing the dumbbells together by shrugging the shoulders forward
Dropping the arms quickly instead of controlling the arc

name: Dumbbell Fly On Exercise Ball
description: A chest isolation move done on an exercise ball, lowering dumbbells in a wide arc and bringing them back together over the chest.
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported by the ball. Extend your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other. Bend your elbows slightly and lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest. Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement and squeeze your chest muscles as you bring the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag below the torso
Turning the movement into a press by bending the elbows too much
Lowering the dumbbells far below chest level
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
description: A shoulder isolation exercise where you lift dumbbells straight forward from your thighs to shoulder height.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your thighs. Keeping your arms straight, exhale and lift the dumbbells in front of you until they are at shoulder level. Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the dumbbells up with the hips or torso.
Lifting the weights higher than shoulder level.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
Bending the elbows more as the weights rise.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
description: A front-loaded squat holding one dumbbell at the chest to train the quads, glutes, and legs through a controlled deep squat.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Keeping your chest up and core engaged, lower your body down into a squat position by pushing your hips back and bending your knees. Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Letting the dumbbell drift away from the chest
Heels lifting off the floor at the bottom
Knees collapsing inward during the squat
Folding the chest forward instead of staying upright

name: Dumbbell Hammer Grip Incline Bench Row
description: A back-focused row performed chest-down on an incline bench with dumbbells and a neutral (hammer) grip.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, neutral grip. Row the weights up toward your hips, squeezing your lats, then lower with control.
aliases: dumbbell reverse grip incline bench one arm row

name: Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
description: A pressing exercise on an incline bench using dumbbells to train the upper chest, shoulders, and triceps.
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle. Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed firmly against the bench. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward, and lift them to shoulder height. Slowly lower the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle. Push the dumbbells back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Letting the dumbbells drift toward the face
Bouncing the dumbbells off the chest position
Arching the lower back off the bench

name: Dumbbell Incline Curl
description: A seated biceps curl on an incline bench that trains the biceps through a long range with dumbbells.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward. Rest your upper arms on the incline bench and let your elbows hang down, fully extending your arms. Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps. Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the dumbbells to start the curl
Letting the elbows drift forward as the weights rise
Stopping short instead of fully lowering the dumbbells
Bending the wrists back while curling

name: Dumbbell Incline Fly
description: A chest isolation exercise done on an incline bench by opening the arms wide with dumbbells and squeezing them back together.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle. Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Lie back on the bench and press the dumbbells up to the starting position, directly above your chest. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest. Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows like a press
Lowering the dumbbells far below chest level
Letting the dumbbells drift behind the shoulders
Clanging the dumbbells together at the top

name: Dumbbell Incline Fly On Exercise Ball
description: A chest isolation exercise done with dumbbells while supported on an exercise ball at an incline angle.
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle. Sit on an exercise ball and roll forward until your upper back is resting on the incline bench. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest. Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Straightening the elbows and turning the move into a press
Lowering the dumbbells too far below chest level
Bouncing the hips or letting the ball roll around
Bringing the dumbbells up unevenly or clanking them together

name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Curl
description: A seated incline curl with a neutral grip that targets the biceps and forearms while limiting body swing.
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso and arms fully extended. Keep your back against the bench and your feet flat on the floor. While keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps. Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the dumbbells up with the torso
Letting the elbows drift forward during the curl
Turning the palms up at the top

name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Press
description: An incline dumbbell press with a neutral grip that trains the upper chest, shoulders, and triceps.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs. Lie back on the bench and position the dumbbells at shoulder level with your palms facing each other. Press the dumbbells up and away from your body until your arms are fully extended. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Letting the dumbbells drift back over the face
Banging the dumbbells together at the top
Arching the lower back and lifting the hips
aliases: incline press with palms facing in

name: Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral Raise
description: A chest-supported dumbbell raise that targets the rear delts by lifting the arms out to the sides on an incline bench.
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle. Sit on the bench with your chest against the backrest and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Extend your arms straight down with your palms facing each other. Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the dumbbells up with momentum
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Straightening the elbows into a wide row
Lifting the arms far past shoulder height

name: Dumbbell Incline Row
description: A chest-supported dumbbell row on an incline bench that targets the upper back while limiting body momentum.
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle. Grab a dumbbell in each hand and sit on the bench with your chest against the incline. Extend your arms fully, allowing the dumbbells to hang straight down from your shoulders. Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Yanking the dumbbells with body momentum
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Lifting the chest off the bench at the top

name: Dumbbell Incline Shrug
description: A chest-supported shrug on an incline bench using dumbbells to target the upper traps with minimal body momentum.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand. Place your feet flat on the ground and let your arms hang straight down with your palms facing your body. Keeping your arms straight, shrug your shoulders up towards your ears as high as possible. Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows and turning the rep into a row
Rolling the shoulders forward or backward at the top
Lifting the chest off the bench to move the weight
Using momentum and dropping quickly between reps

name: Dumbbell Incline Triceps Extension
description: A seated incline dumbbell triceps exercise where you bend and straighten the elbows to move the weights behind and above the head.
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards. Extend your arms fully overhead, keeping your elbows close to your head. Lower the dumbbells behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary. Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbells back to the starting position by extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Elbows flare wide out to the sides.
Upper arms drift backward and turn it into a press.
Lowering only a few inches behind the head.
Arching the low back off the bench.

name: Dumbbell Iron Cross
description: A shoulder isolation exercise where you raise dumbbells out to the sides to train the delts.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground, forming a T shape with your body. Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start each rep
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Lifting the dumbbells higher than shoulder level
Straightening the elbows completely and locking the arms
aliases: dumbbell arm raise to the side

name: Dumbbell Kickback
description: A bent-over triceps isolation exercise where you extend dumbbells behind you while keeping the upper arms still.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight. Bring your upper arms close to your sides, with your elbows bent at a 90-degree angle. Extend your arms straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement. Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the dumbbells with the shoulders or torso
Letting the elbows drift away from the ribs
Dropping the upper arms during the set
Snapping the weights down instead of lowering slowly

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: A shoulder isolation exercise where you lift dumbbells out to the sides to target the lateral delts.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body. Keep your back straight and engage your core. Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Swinging the torso to heave the dumbbells upward
Lifting the hands well above shoulder height
Straightening the elbows and turning it into a front swing

name: Dumbbell Lunge
description: A lower-body exercise where you hold dumbbells and step into alternating lunges to train the glutes, quads, and legs.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Take a step forward with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge position. Keep your back straight and your chest up as you lower your body. Push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Repeat with your left leg. Alternate legs for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Taking too short a step so the front knee shoots far past the toes.
Leaning the torso forward as you lower into the lunge.
Letting the front heel lift off the floor.
Pushing off the back foot instead of driving through the front leg.

name: Dumbbell Lying Alternate Extension
description: A lying triceps isolation exercise where you lower one dumbbell at a time toward your forehead and extend the elbow back to the top.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. Lower one dumbbell down towards your head, bending at the elbow, while keeping the other arm extended. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then raise the dumbbell back up to the starting position. Repeat with the other arm, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Elbows flare wide as the dumbbell lowers
Upper arms drift backward instead of staying upright
The non-working arm drops or bends
Turning it into a press from the chest

name: Dumbbell Lying Hammer Press
description: A flat bench dumbbell press done with a neutral grip to train the chest, triceps, and shoulders.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other and arms extended straight up. Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle. Press the dumbbells back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Elbows flare straight out to the sides.
Dumbbells drift toward the face instead of staying over the chest.
Wrists bend back under the dumbbells.
Lowering too fast and bouncing at the bottom.
aliases: dumbbell chest press with palms facing

name: Dumbbell Lying Leg Curl
description: A hamstring isolation exercise where a dumbbell is held between the feet during leg curls.
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell held securely between your feet. Flex your knees to bring the dumbbell up toward your glutes, then lower with control.

name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row
description: A chest-supported dumbbell row variation that targets the rear delts and upper back by pulling the elbows out wide.
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards. Extend your arms straight down towards the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. Engaging your back muscles, lift the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Pulling the elbows close to the ribs like a regular row
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Lifting the chest off the bench to move the weights
Swinging the dumbbells instead of lowering them with control

name: Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension
description: A lying dumbbell triceps exercise where you bend and straighten the elbows to lower the weights toward the forehead and press them back up.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body. Lower the dumbbells down towards your forehead, bending your elbows. Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
