commonMistakes: Elbows flare out wide as the dumbbells lower.
Upper arms drift backward or forward during the rep.
Dumbbells drop too low behind the head instead of beside the forehead.
Wrists bend back instead of staying straight.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise
description: A single-arm shoulder isolation exercise where you raise a dumbbell out to the side to train the lateral delts.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing your body. Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise. Raise the dumbbell to the side, keeping your arm straight and your palm facing down. Continue lifting until your arm is parallel to the ground. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the working shoulder up toward the ear
Swinging the torso or leaning to start the lift
Raising the dumbbell higher than shoulder height

name: Dumbbell One Arm Zottman Preacher Curl
description: A single-arm preacher curl variation that adds a wrist rotation to train the biceps and forearms through both the lift and lowering phase.
instructions: Sit on a preacher curl bench and hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip. Rest your upper arm on the preacher bench pad, allowing your arm to fully extend. Curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary. At the top of the curl, rotate your wrist so that your palm faces up. Slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position, rotating your wrist back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
formCues: Lower slowly on the way down
commonMistakes: Upper arm lifting off the preacher pad
Swinging the dumbbell instead of curling it
Dropping the weight quickly on the lowering phase
Rotating the wrist too early before reaching the top
aliases: one-arm biceps curl on preacher bench

name: Dumbbell One-Arm Triceps Extension
description: An isolation exercise for the triceps performed one arm at a time, with a dumbbell overhead.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell overhead with one arm fully extended. Lower the dumbbell by bending the elbow, then extend the arm back up to starting position, keeping upper arm still.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Wrist Curl
description: A seated forearm isolation exercise where the wrists curl dumbbells upward with the forearms supported on a bench.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forearms resting on the bench and your palms facing up, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Allow your wrists to hang over the edge of the bench. Slowly curl your wrists upward, squeezing your forearms at the top of the movement. Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Lifting the forearms off the bench during the curl.
Swinging the dumbbells instead of moving only the wrists.
Using partial range and stopping before the wrists fully lower.
Bending the elbows to help raise the weight.

name: Dumbbell Palm Rotational Bent Over Row
description: A bent-over dumbbell row where you rotate your palms during the pull to train the upper back, biceps, and forearms.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip. Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent. Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing your body. Engage your core and pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body. As you pull the dumbbells up, rotate your palms so they face away from your body. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement. Slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position, rotating your palms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as you hinge forward
Standing up taller to swing the dumbbells
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Letting the wrists curl instead of rotating the forearms

name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl Over Exercise Ball
description: A single-arm biceps curl done with the upper arm braced against an exercise ball to limit cheating and isolate the elbow flexors.
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip, resting your elbow on the exercise ball. Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder. Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
commonMistakes: Elbow slides or lifts off the ball during the curl.
Shoulder rolls forward to help raise the dumbbell.
Wrist bends back or curls inward at the top.
Body rocks on the ball to create momentum.
aliases: biceps curl with elbow on ball

name: Dumbbell Pronate-grip Triceps Extension
description: A seated overhead triceps exercise using one dumbbell held with both hands to bend and straighten the elbows.
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your back straight and feet flat on the ground. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms facing down, and extend your arms straight up overhead. Keeping your upper arms close to your head and elbows pointing forward, slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows. Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Elbows flare wide out to the sides.
Upper arms drift backward and move during the rep.
Lower back arches as the weight goes overhead.
The dumbbell drops too low and bumps the upper back.

name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
description: A chest-supported biceps curl on an incline bench that limits body swing and keeps tension on the arms.
instructions: Adjust the bench to a 45-degree incline. Lie face down on the bench with your chest and stomach resting against it. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended. Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps. Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench to swing the weights
Letting the elbows drift forward during the curl
Cutting the rep short and not fully lowering the dumbbells
Bending the wrists back instead of keeping them neutral

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
description: A bent-over dumbbell row variation that targets the rear delts by pulling the elbows out wide to the sides.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your core engaged. Extend your arms straight down towards the floor, with a slight bend in your elbows. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as you hinge forward.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
Pulling the dumbbells straight back close to the ribs.
Swinging the torso to start each rep.

name: Dumbbell Seated Calf Raise
description: A seated calf exercise using a dumbbell on the thighs to train ankle plantarflexion through a full range of motion.
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the ground and a dumbbell resting on your thighs. Place the balls of your feet on a raised surface such as a step or block, with your heels hanging off the edge. Hold onto the dumbbell for stability. Raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the heels at the bottom instead of lowering under control.
Rolling the ankles inward or outward as the heels rise.
Placing the dumbbell too close to the knees so it slides during the set.
Using a very short range of motion and not dropping the heels below the step.

name: Dumbbell Seated Front Raise
description: A seated shoulder isolation exercise where you lift dumbbells straight in front to shoulder height to train the front delts.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs. Keep your back straight and core engaged. Raise the dumbbells in front of you, with your palms facing down, until they are at shoulder level. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Leaning the torso back to swing the dumbbells up
Raising the dumbbells above shoulder height
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Dropping the weights quickly on the way down

name: Dumbbell Seated Kickback
description: A seated triceps isolation exercise where you hinge forward and extend dumbbells back by straightening the elbows.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees slightly and lean forward from your hips, keeping your back straight. Bring your upper arms close to your sides and keep your elbows bent at a 90-degree angle. Extend your arms straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement. Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the dumbbells with the shoulders
Letting the elbows drift away from the torso
Dropping the upper arms during the rep
Rounding the back while leaning forward

name: Dumbbell Seated Lateral Raise
description: A seated shoulder isolation exercise where you raise dumbbells out to the sides to target the delts.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs. Keep your back straight and core engaged. Raise the dumbbells to your sides with a slight bend in your elbows, until your arms are parallel to the ground. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start the lift
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Lifting the dumbbells higher than shoulder level
Straightening the elbows into a stiff arm

name: Dumbbell Seated Neutral Wrist Curl
description: A seated forearm isolation exercise where you curl dumbbells by bending at the wrists with a neutral grip.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing the dumbbells to hang down. Keeping your wrists in a neutral position, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Lifting the forearms off the thighs to swing the dumbbells up
Turning the palms up or down during the curl
Bouncing the dumbbells at the bottom
Using the shoulders or elbows to help the movement

name: Dumbbell Seated Preacher Curl
description: A seated single-arm biceps curl done against a preacher pad to isolate the elbow flexors and limit body momentum.
instructions: Sit on a preacher curl bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip, resting your upper arm against the preacher pad. Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder. Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
commonMistakes: Upper arm lifting off the pad during the curl
Swinging the dumbbell instead of moving smoothly
Stopping short and not lowering near full extension
Bending the wrist back as the dumbbell rises
aliases: one-arm biceps curl on preacher bench

name: Dumbbell Seated Triceps Extension
description: A seated overhead dumbbell triceps exercise where you lower the weight behind your head and extend your elbows to press it back up.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground. Hold a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up overhead. Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arms close to your ears. Pause for a moment, then straighten your arms and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Elbows flare wide out to the sides.
Lower back arches as the weight goes overhead.
Upper arms drift backward and forward during the rep.
The dumbbell drops too low with no control behind the head.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
description: An isolation exercise where you hold dumbbells at your sides and lift your shoulders up to train the trapezius muscles.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Keep your arms straight and let the dumbbells hang by your sides. Raise your shoulders as high as possible, as if you are trying to touch your ears with your shoulders. Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Rolling the shoulders in circles instead of lifting straight up and down.
Bending the elbows and turning the move into an upright row.
Leaning the torso back or forward to swing the dumbbells.
Jutting the head forward as the shoulders rise.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: A standing oblique exercise where you hold one dumbbell and bend your torso sideways under control.
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang down by your side. Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, slowly bend sideways at the waist towards the opposite side of the dumbbell, lowering the weight as far as you comfortably can. Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso as you bend
Using momentum to swing back up

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Calf Raise
description: A single-leg calf exercise using a dumbbell and step to strengthen the calves through a full ankle range of motion.
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step or platform with your heels hanging off and your toes on the step. Hold a dumbbell in one hand and place your other hand on a wall or railing for support. Raise your heel as high as possible, lifting your body up onto your toes. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down below the step. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom instead of lowering under control
Rolling the ankle inward or outward during the raise
Bending the standing knee to help drive up
Using the support hand to pull the body upward

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Squat
description: A one-leg squat holding dumbbells that challenges the glutes, quads, balance, and lower-body control.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Extend one leg forward and keep it off the ground throughout the exercise. Bend your standing leg and lower your body down as if sitting back into a chair. Keep your chest up and your back straight. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heel to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
commonMistakes: Letting the lifted foot touch the floor between reps
Rounding the back at the bottom
Dropping too fast and losing balance

name: Dumbbell Squat
description: A squat holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides to train the glutes, quads, and legs.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Keeping your chest up and core engaged, lower your body down by bending at the knees and hips, as if sitting back into a chair. Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward on the way down or up.
Rising onto the toes and lifting the heels off the floor.
Rounding the upper or lower back at the bottom.
Dropping the chest forward so the dumbbells swing ahead of the legs.

name: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise
description: A standing calf exercise where you hold dumbbells at your sides and raise your heels to train the calves and ankles.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Raise your heels off the ground as high as possible, using your calves. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bouncing at the bottom instead of lowering under control
Rolling the ankles outward or inward
Bending the knees to turn it into a squat
Leaning the torso forward as the heels lift

name: Dumbbell Stiff Leg Deadlift
description: A hip-hinge deadlift with dumbbells that emphasizes the hamstrings and glutes while keeping only a slight knee bend.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip. Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, hinge at the hips and lower the dumbbells towards the ground, allowing a slight bend in your knees. Lower the dumbbells until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, then squeeze your glutes and push through your heels to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees too much and turning it into a squat
Letting the dumbbells drift away from the legs
Rounding the lower back on the way down
Looking up and cranking the neck

name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
description: A lower body exercise using a dumbbell in a sumo stance to target the glutes, quads, and adductors.
instructions: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed out, holding a dumbbell vertically with both hands. Squat down by pushing hips back and knees out, then return to standing.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
description: A standing shoulder and upper-trap exercise where you pull dumbbells up the front of your body with elbows leading.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip. Let the dumbbells hang in front of your thighs, with your arms fully extended. Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, exhale and lift the dumbbells straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows. Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Pulling the dumbbells all the way to the chin
Letting the wrists bend sharply at the top
Swinging the torso to start the lift
Hands rising higher than the elbows

name: Dynamic Chest Stretch
description: A rhythmic arm movement to increase chest mobility and warm up the pectoral muscles.
instructions: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended at shoulder height. Swing your arms in a controlled, hugging motion across your chest and then open wide, repeating rhythmically to stretch and activate the chest.

name: Elliptical Trainer
description: A low-impact cardio exercise using a standing elliptical machine for total body endurance and aerobic gains.
instructions: Step onto the elliptical machine and grasp the moving handles. Begin moving feet in an elliptical motion, engaging both the lower and upper body by pushing and pulling the handles as you stride.
commonMistakes: Leaning too far forward or backward
Relying only on legs or arms

name: Exercise Ball Sit-Up
description: A core exercise where sit-ups are performed while stabilizing on a Swiss ball, increasing abdominal activation.
instructions: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward until the ball is under your lower back. Cross your arms over your chest or place hands behind your head, then contract your abs to lift your torso, performing a sit-up. Lower yourself back down slowly and repeat.
commonMistakes: Ball not positioned under lower back

name: Exercise Ball Spinal Stretch
description: A gentle back extension and stretch performed by draping the body over an exercise ball to mobilize the spine.
instructions: Sit on a stability ball and carefully roll down until your back is resting on the ball. Extend your arms overhead and allow your spine to gently arch over the ball, stretching the entire length of your back. Hold the stretch, breathing deeply.
aliases: Stretching - Spinal Stretch On Exercise Ball

name: EZ Bar Biceps Curl
description: Classic biceps curl using an EZ barbell to build arm mass with ergonomic grip.
instructions: Stand upright holding an EZ bar with hands on the angled grips, arms fully extended. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping elbows close to your torso. Squeeze the biceps at the top, then slowly lower to the starting position.

name: EZ Bar Lying Triceps Extension
description: Lying triceps extension using EZ bar to target triceps with reduced wrist strain.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding the EZ bar with arms extended above your chest. Bend elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, upper arms stationary. Extend arms back up, focusing on triceps contraction, and repeat for desired reps.
commonMistakes: Lowering bar too far past head

name: EZ Barbell Anti Gravity Press
description: A standing overhead press using an EZ bar to train the delts, triceps, and upper chest through a full pressing range.
instructions: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and holding the ez barbell with an overhand grip. Raise the barbell to shoulder height, keeping your elbows slightly bent and your palms facing forward. Press the barbell overhead, extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell back to shoulder height and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Leaning back hard and turning it into an incline press
Pressing the bar out in front instead of overhead
Flaring the elbows too far out from the start
Lowering the bar too fast and bouncing at the shoulders
aliases: overhead shoulder press with EZ bar

name: Feet and Ankles Rotation Stretch
description: A mobility exercise involving circular ankle movements that target the calves and improve ankle flexibility.
instructions: Sit or stand with one leg lifted and rotate your foot at the ankle in slow, controlled circles, first one direction and then the other. Focus on full range of motion to stretch and warm up lower leg muscles and joints.

name: Feet and Ankles Stretch
description: A stretch to increase flexibility and mobility in the feet and ankle muscles.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended. Point and flex your toes to stretch the ankle and foot muscles. Hold the stretch for several seconds and repeat as needed.
formCues: Hold gentle tension, do not force
commonMistakes: Overstretching or forcing range of motion

name: Flat Bench Cable Fly
description: A chest isolation exercise using cables while lying on a flat bench for continuous tension.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench positioned between two low cable pulleys. Grab the handles with arms extended and a slight bend in the elbows, then bring your hands together in a wide arc before returning to the start position.
aliases: Cable Lying Fly, Flat Bench Cable Fly

name: Flexion Leg Sit-Up Stretch
description: A stretch that combines trunk flexion with leg movement to lengthen the abdominals and hip flexors.
instructions: Start lying on your back with knees bent. Flex your spine as you perform a sit-up, reaching toward your knees. Pause in the top position for a stretch before lowering back down.

name: Floor Crunch
description: A basic abdominal crunch performed lying on the floor to strengthen the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place your hands behind your head or across your chest, engage your core, and curl your shoulders up toward your knees.

name: Front Plank
description: An isometric core stability exercise performed in a prone position to strengthen the abdominals and stabilize the entire body.
instructions: Start in a prone position with forearms and toes on the ground. Engage your core, keep your body in a straight line from head to heels, and hold the position for the desired amount of time without allowing hips to rise or sag.

name: Front Toe Touch Stretch
description: A classic stretch where you bend forward to touch your toes, lengthening the hamstrings and lower back.
instructions: Stand or sit with legs straight. Hinge at the hips and reach forward toward your toes, keeping your spine long. Hold at your end range, feeling a stretch in the back of your legs.
formCues: Keep head in line with spine

name: Glute Bridge
description: A floor-based exercise that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings by lifting the hips.
instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent and feet flat on the floor hip-width apart. Drive through your heels to lift hips off the ground, squeezing the glutes at the top, then lower back down with control.

name: Hammer Curl
description: A standing dumbbell curl with palms facing each other that also trains the forearms.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your sides. Keeping your elbows close to your torso, curl the weights toward your shoulders without rotating your wrists, then lower under control.

name: Hanging Leg Hip Raise
description: A hanging core exercise where you raise your knees and curl your hips upward to train the abs and hip flexors.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you. Engage your core and lift your legs up by flexing your hips and knees until your thighs are parallel to the ground. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the body to start each rep
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Dropping the legs quickly on the way down
Only lifting the knees halfway with no hip curl

name: Hanging Straight Leg Raise
description: A core exercise performed while hanging, lifting straight legs to target the abdominals and hip flexors.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, keeping your body steady. Contract your core and raise your legs, keeping them straight, until they're parallel to the ground or higher. Lower your legs with control and repeat.

name: Hip Circles Stretch
description: A dynamic stretch to increase mobility in the hips by performing circular leg movements.
instructions: Stand upright and place your hands on your hips. Lift one knee and move your leg in a controlled circular motion from the hip joint, reversing direction as needed; repeat with the other leg.

name: Hip Extension Stretch
description: A stretch focused on extending the hip to target tight hip flexors and anterior hips.
instructions: Lie on your stomach with legs outstretched and hands placed underneath your shoulders. Gently press up through your palms, extending the hips and lifting your torso without overextending the low back. Maintain a gentle stretch and hold.

name: Hip Flexor and Quadriceps Stretch
description: A stretch that lengthens the hip flexors and quadriceps by using a kneeling or lunge position.
instructions: Start in a half-kneeling (lunge) position with one knee on the floor and the other foot planted in front. Gently shift hips forward while keeping torso upright, feeling the stretch in the front of the rear leg and thigh. Hold, then switch sides.
commonMistakes: Letting front knee go past toes
aliases: Stretching - Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
intermediate hip flexor and quad stretch

name: Incline Leg Hip Raise
description: A core exercise where legs and hips are raised while lying on an incline, targeting the lower abdominals.
instructions: Lie on your back on an incline bench and hold the handles or bench for stability. Keeping legs straight, lift them until your hips come off the bench, then lower slowly.

name: Incline Push-Up
description: A push-up variation with hands elevated, reducing resistance on the chest and triceps.
instructions: Place your hands on an elevated surface like a bench, stand with feet extended behind you and body straight. Lower your chest toward the surface, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle, then press up to starting position.

name: Inverted Row Between Chairs
description: A bodyweight pulling exercise performed using a bar or sturdy broomstick supported between two chairs.
instructions: Set up a sturdy bar or stick horizontally between two secure chairs. Lie on your back underneath the bar, grasp it with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, and keep your body straight from head to heels. Pull your chest toward the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then lower yourself back down with control.

name: Inverted Row With Straps
description: A bodyweight upper-back row using suspension straps, pulling your chest toward the handles while keeping your body straight.
instructions: Set up a suspension trainer or straps at chest height. Stand facing the anchor point and grab the handles with an overhand grip. Walk your feet forward, leaning back until your body is at an angle. Keep your body straight and engage your core. Pull your chest towards the handles, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Hips sag or pike instead of staying straight
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Pulling with bent wrists and loose handles
Letting the body drop quickly on the way down

name: Iron Cross Stretch
description: A lying rotational stretch that improves spinal mobility and stretches the obliques and lower back.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms spread out in a 'T' position. Lift one leg straight up and sweep it across your body to the opposite side, letting it fall toward the floor while keeping your shoulders flat. Hold the position, feeling a stretch through your torso and hip.

name: Jackknife
description: A Pilates core exercise involving lifting hips and legs up and overhead to strengthen the abdominals.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with arms by your sides and legs together. Lift your legs towards the ceiling and roll your hips off the mat, supporting your back lightly with your hands if needed, then lower with control.

name: Jackknife Floor
description: A dynamic ab exercise where you simultaneously raise legs and torso to touch in a 'V' position.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with arms and legs extended. Simultaneously lift your arms, head, and legs, bringing your hands to meet your shins or feet at the top, then lower back down with control.
commonMistakes: Bending knees or elbows too much

name: Jackknife Split Crunch
description: A crunch variation combining a V-up with a leg split to target the abs and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and arms overhead. Simultaneously lift your torso and legs while spreading your feet apart (splitting legs) and reaching your hands towards your feet. Lower back to the starting position with control.

name: Jump Rope
description: A cardio exercise where you turn a rope with your hands and perform repeated small jumps as it passes under your feet.
instructions: Hold the handles of the jump rope with your hands, palms facing inward. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Swing the rope over your head and jump over it as it comes towards your feet. Land softly on the balls of your feet and repeat the jump as the rope comes around again. Continue jumping for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the arms in big circles instead of using the wrists
Jumping too high off the floor on each rep
Landing flat-footed or with stiff knees
Letting the hands drift wide away from the hips

name: Jump Step-Up
description: A plyometric exercise involving stepping and jumping onto a raised surface to build leg power and coordination.
instructions: Stand in front of a box or platform. Step onto the box with one foot, then explosively jump up, driving through the working leg. Land softly and return to the starting position, alternating legs if desired.
formCues: Drive explosively through the lead leg
commonMistakes: Not using full range of motion

name: Jumping Jack
description: A dynamic total-body movement for cardiovascular and muscular endurance.
instructions: Begin standing with feet together and arms at sides. Jump feet outward while raising arms overhead, then reverse to starting position in a single fluid motion.

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
description: A hip hinge movement using a kettlebell from the floor to standing, building posterior chain and grip strength.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, kettlebell between your feet. Hinge at the hips, bend knees and keep your back flat as you grip the kettlebell handle with both hands. Drive through your heels, extend hips and stand tall with the kettlebell, then reverse the movement to return to start.

name: Kneeling Back Rotation Stretch
description: A mobility stretch that improves thoracic spine rotation while kneeling, also opening the chest and shoulders.
instructions: Begin in a quadruped or kneeling lunge position. Place one hand behind your head and rotate your torso to open the chest, aiming elbow upward. Hold briefly and return, then repeat on the other side.

name: Kneeling Lat Stretch
description: A floor stretch to lengthen the latissimus dorsi and improve shoulder mobility.
instructions: Kneel on the ground, sit your hips back towards your heels, and reach both arms straight out in front of you on the floor. Push your chest down and feel the stretch along each side of your back. Hold, then optionally move hands to each side to target one lat more intensely.

name: Kneeling Triceps Stretch
description: A static stretch targeting the triceps and lats by flexing the elbow overhead while kneeling.
instructions: Kneel on the floor and reach one arm overhead, bending the elbow to let your hand touch your upper back. With the opposite hand, gently press on the bent elbow to increase the stretch.

name: Landmine 180
description: A rotating landmine core exercise where you swing the barbell side to side using your hips, shoulders, and obliques.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell with both hands in front of your chest. Bend your knees slightly and rotate your torso to the right, swinging the barbell down towards your right hip. As you reach the bottom of the movement, quickly reverse the motion and rotate your torso to the left, swinging the barbell up and across your body towards your left shoulder. Continue this twisting motion, alternating sides, for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Move the bar in an arc
commonMistakes: Twisting only the arms while the torso stays still
Letting the lower back arch as the bar moves
Locking the knees and staying flat-footed
Jerking the bar instead of controlling the arc

name: Leg Raise Crunch
description: An ab exercise combining a crunch with a leg raise to emphasize upper and lower abdominals.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms at your sides and legs extended. Raise your legs and torso together, crunching your upper body forward as you lift your legs off the floor, then slowly return to starting position.
formCues: Keep lower back pressed to floor

name: Leg Raise with Hip Lift
description: A core exercise combining a leg raise with a hip lift to target the lower abdominals.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides. Raise your legs until they are perpendicular to the floor, then lift your hips off the ground by contracting your lower abs. Lower back slowly with control.
aliases: lying leg raise with hip lift

name: Lever Back Extension
description: A machine-based trunk extension that trains the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings by moving your torso against resistance.
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body size and range of motion. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and your feet secured. Place your hands on the handles or grip bars. Engage your core and slowly lean forward, allowing your back to round slightly. Pause for a moment at the bottom position, feeling a stretch in your lower back. Using your back muscles, slowly raise your torso back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Using momentum and bouncing out of the bottom position
Pushing through a short, rushed range of motion
Letting the feet lift or shift on the platform
Hyperextending far past upright at the top

name: Lever High Row
description: A chest-supported machine row that trains the upper back by pulling handles from in front of you toward your torso.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and foot platform to a comfortable position. Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the foot platform. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Keep your back straight and engage your core. Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears as you pull
Leaning off the chest pad to move the weight
Letting the handles slam forward between reps
Bending the wrists back instead of keeping them neutral

name: Lever Horizontal Leg Press
description: A horizontal plate-loaded machine exercise targeting the entire thigh, especially the quadriceps.
instructions: Sit on the leg press machine with your feet hip-width apart on the platform. Press the platform away by extending your legs, but avoid locking your knees, then lower slowly back to the starting position.
formCues: Keep lower back pressed into seat

name: Lever Incline Hammer Chest Press
description: A machine-based incline chest press emphasizing the upper chest and shoulders.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with your upper chest when seated. Grip the handles firmly and press them up and slightly forward, focusing on squeezing your upper chest. Return to the starting position under control after a brief pause.

name: Lever Kneeling Leg Curl
description: A machine hamstring exercise done kneeling, curling the lower legs toward the glutes by bending the knees.
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body and select the desired weight. Kneel on the machine facing downwards, with your knees resting on the pad and your feet secured under the footpads. Grasp the handles or the sides of the machine for stability. Keeping your upper body stationary, exhale and curl your legs up towards your glutes by flexing your knees. Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your hamstrings. Inhale and slowly lower your legs back to the starting position, fully extending your knees. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Move slowly on the way down
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the pad during the curl
Swinging the legs to start each rep
Stopping short and not straightening the knees at the bottom
Letting the ankles slip out of the pads

name: Lever Lateral Raise
description: A machine shoulder isolation exercise where you lift your arms out to the sides to target the lateral delts.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the pad. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms straight. Exhale and raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor. Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower your arms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Swinging or bouncing the weight at the bottom
Lifting the arms far above shoulder height
Letting the back come off the pad

name: Lever Leg Extension
description: A seated machine exercise that strengthens the quadriceps by extending the knees against a padded lever.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and backrest of the machine to fit your body. Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the footpad. Grasp the handles or sidebars for stability. Extend your legs forward by straightening your knees, lifting the weight. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Knees sit too far forward or behind the machine pivot.
Swinging the weight up with momentum.
Locking the knees hard at the top.
Lifting the hips or lower back off the seat.

name: Lever Lying Chest Press
description: A plate-loaded machine press mimicking the bench press to target the entire chest safely.
instructions: Lie back on the lever chest press machine, gripping the handles just outside shoulder-width. Press the levers forward and upward by extending your arms fully, focusing on squeezing your chest, then return with control to the starting position.

name: Lever Lying Leg Curl
description: A machine hamstring exercise done face down by bending the knees to curl a padded lever toward the glutes.
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body and select the desired weight. Lie face down on the machine with your legs straight and your heels against the padded lever. Grasp the handles or the sides of the machine for stability. Keeping your upper body stationary, exhale and curl your legs up as far as possible without lifting your hips off the pad. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your hamstrings. Inhale and slowly lower the lever back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Move slow on the way down
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the pad at the top
Using momentum to swing the pad upward
Stopping short and not fully lowering the pad
Feet turning sharply inward or outward during the curl

name: Lever Preacher Curl
description: A machine biceps curl done with the upper arms braced on a preacher pad to isolate elbow flexion.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the leverage machine. Place your upper arms on the pad and grip the handles with an underhand grip. Keep your back straight and your elbows positioned on the pad. Exhale and curl your forearms towards your upper arms, contracting your biceps. Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps. Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Upper arms lifting off the pad as the handles rise
Using the shoulders or rocking the torso to start the curl
Letting the weight drop quickly on the way down
Bending the wrists back instead of keeping them straight

name: Lever Reverse Hyperextension
description: A machine glute and hamstring exercise where you raise your legs behind you while lying face down on a pad.
instructions: Adjust the leverage machine to fit your body and secure your feet in the foot pads. Lie face down on the machine with your upper body hanging off the edge and your hips resting on the pad. Cross your arms over your chest or place them behind your head. Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your legs upward until they are parallel to the ground. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Swinging the legs up with momentum
Arching the lower back at the top
Letting the hips slide off the pad
Bending and straightening the knees during each rep

name: Lever Reverse T-Bar Row
description: A chest-supported leverage machine row using an overhand grip to train the upper back, biceps, and forearms.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and footplate position on the leverage machine. Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the footplate. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Keep your back straight and engage your core. Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Bouncing the chest off the pad to move the handles
Letting the upper back round at the start
Yanking the weight and dropping it back fast

name: Lever Seated Calf Raise
description: A seated machine calf exercise where you raise and lower your heels to train the soleus through ankle plantarflexion.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your knees are slightly bent and your feet are flat on the footplate. Place your toes on the footplate with your heels hanging off the edge. Grasp the handles or the sides of the seat for stability. Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom instead of lowering under control.
Letting the knees shift up and down during the rep.
Rolling the feet outward or inward on the platform.
Using only a short top-half range of motion.

name: Lever Seated Crunch
description: A machine exercise that isolates and strengthens the abdominal muscles through spinal flexion.
instructions: Sit in the lever crunch machine and grasp the handles or position yourself according to machine design. Contract your abs to flex your spine forward, bringing your chest toward your knees, then return slowly to the starting position.

name: Lever Seated Dip
description: A machine-based dip that targets the triceps, chest, and shoulders in a seated position.
instructions: Sit on the dip machine with your back against the pad, grip the handles, and position your feet flat on the platform. Press the handles downward by extending your arms, keeping your elbows close to your body, then return to the starting position in a controlled motion.

name: Lever Seated Hip Abduction
description: A seated machine exercise where you press your legs outward against pads to train the hip abductors and outer glutes.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your knees are at a 90-degree angle. Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the footrests. Place your hands on the side handles for stability. Engage your abductors and slowly push your legs apart, away from the midline of your body. Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly bring your legs back together to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Leaning the torso forward or rocking back to move the weight.
Letting the legs snap back together on the return.
Lifting the hips off the seat at the widest point.
Turning the feet excessively to cheat the movement.

name: Lever Seated Hip Adduction
description: A seated machine exercise that trains the inner thighs by bringing the legs together against resistance.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the backrest. Place your feet on the footrests and grasp the handles for stability. Engage your adductor muscles and slowly bring your legs together, squeezing your inner thighs. Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward or lifting the lower back off the pad.
Letting the pads fly open on the way back.
Using short, bouncing reps instead of controlled motion.
Turning the feet and knees excessively to force the movement.

name: Lever Seated Leg Curl
description: A seated machine hamstring exercise where you bend your knees to pull a padded lever downward.
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body and sit on it with your back against the backrest. Place your lower legs under the padded lever, just above your ankles. Grasp the handles on the sides of the machine for support. Keeping your upper legs stationary, exhale and curl your legs up as far as possible. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your hamstrings. Inhale and slowly lower the lever back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the seat during the curl.
Using momentum and swinging the pad through the rep.
Letting the knees fully lock out at the top.
Setting the pad too high on the calves instead of above the ankles.

name: Lever Seated Reverse Fly
description: A machine rear-delt exercise where you pull the handles out and back while seated with your chest supported.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms slightly bent. Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the handles back and outward, away from your body. Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Straightening the elbows and turning it into a press
Letting the chest come off the pad
Swinging the handles back with momentum

name: Lever Shrug
description: A machine trap exercise where you lift your shoulders straight up against the handles to train the upper trapezius.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the leverage machine with your back against the pad. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms straight. Keeping your back straight, lift your shoulders up towards your ears as high as possible. Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows and turning it into a row
Rolling the shoulders forward or backward
Leaning the torso to move the weight
Jutting the chin forward as the shoulders rise

name: Lever Standing Calf Raise
description: A machine calf exercise where you raise and lower your heels under shoulder pads to train the calves through ankle movement.
instructions: Adjust the machine to your height and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your shoulders under the pads and hold onto the handles for stability. Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom instead of lowering under control.
Bending the knees noticeably during the raise.
Rolling the ankles inward or outward as the heels lift.
Using a short range and stopping before the heels fully lower.

name: Lever Standing Hip Extension
description: A machine-based hip extension to isolate and strengthen the glutes.
instructions: Position yourself on the standing hip extension machine so one foot is on the lever platform. Brace your core and press the platform straight back using your heel, extending your hip fully. Lower under control and repeat for reps before switching legs.

name: Lever Standing Rear Kick
description: A leverage machine exercise that isolates the glutes with a hip extension rear kick motion.
instructions: Set up at the rear kick lever machine with your working foot on the platform and your chest against the pad. Push the lever backward by extending your hip, squeezing your glutes at the top, then return to the starting position.

name: Lever T-Bar Row
description: A machine row movement that maximizes mid-back and lat development through a horizontal pulling pattern.
instructions: Position yourself on the lever T-bar row machine with chest supported and feet braced. Grip the handles, retract your shoulder blades, and pull the handles toward your torso, squeezing your back muscles. Lower the weight under control with full stretch.

name: Lever Triceps Extension
description: A seated leverage machine exercise where you bend and straighten the elbows to train the triceps.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the pad. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and fully extend your arms in front of you. Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the handles towards your forehead by bending your elbows. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the handles back up to the starting position by extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Elbows flare wide out to the sides.
Shoulders roll forward and the chest collapses.
Handles are dropped quickly toward the head.
Upper arms swing back and forth during the rep.

name: Lying Hip Lift on Stability Ball
description: A hip-thrusting exercise using a stability ball to engage glutes, hamstrings, and core.
instructions: Lie with your upper back and arms on the floor and your feet on a stability ball. Brace your core, drive through your heels, and lift your hips to form a straight line from shoulders to knees, then lower back down with control.

name: Lying Leg Raise
description: A bodyweight exercise that targets the lower abdominal muscles by lifting the legs while lying flat.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and arms at your sides or under your hips for support. Keeping legs straight, raise them toward the ceiling until your hips lift slightly off the floor, then lower them back down without touching the ground.
commonMistakes: Touching feet to ground between reps

name: Lying Quadriceps Stretch
description: A stretch for the quadriceps performed lying on the stomach for maximal knee flexion.
instructions: Lie face down and grasp one ankle behind you, gently pulling the heel toward your glutes while keeping hips down. Feel a stretch in the front thigh and hold without straining the knee.

name: Lying Scissor Kick
description: A core and hip flexor exercise performed while lying flat, alternately raising and lowering legs in a scissor-like motion.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms at your sides, legs extended. Lift both legs slightly off the ground, then alternately move one leg up and the other down in a controlled, fluttering motion.

name: Lying Straight Leg Raise
description: An exercise to isolate the hip flexors and lower abdominals from a supine position.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and arms at your sides. Keeping legs straight and together, lift them to about 90 degrees, then lower under control without letting heels touch the ground.

name: Medicine Ball Wall Sit-Up
description: A dynamic core exercise involving a sit-up while throwing and catching a medicine ball against a wall.
instructions: Sit facing a wall with your knees bent, holding a medicine ball at your chest. Perform a sit-up and, at the top, throw the medicine ball against the wall, catch it as it rebounds, then lower back down and repeat.

name: Middle Back Stretch
description: A static stretch to lengthen the muscles of the thoracic (middle) back region.
instructions: Sit or stand with arms extended in front. Clasp your hands and round your upper back, reaching forward to feel a gentle stretch along your middle back. Hold the position without bouncing.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back instead of rounding the upper back

name: Military Press
description: A standing barbell press that builds overall shoulder strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip. Press the bar overhead by extending your arms fully, keeping your core tight and avoiding excessive lower back arch. Lower the bar to the starting position under control.

name: Neck Side Stretch
description: A gentle static stretch that targets the side muscles of the neck, improving mobility and reducing tension.
instructions: Sit or stand upright, keeping good posture. Gently tilt your head toward one shoulder until a stretch is felt along the opposite side of the neck, holding for a set duration before switching sides.
commonMistakes: Turning the head instead of tilting

name: Old School Reverse Extensions
description: This bodyweight movement isolates the triceps by extending the elbows while lying face down.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or bench with arms bent and hands under shoulders. Extend your arms straight back by pressing your palms into the ground or lifting them off the ground, fully straightening your elbows and contracting your triceps. Lower back down under control.

name: Otis-Up
description: A sit-up variation holding a weight at arm’s length overhead to increase abdominal engagement.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a weight plate or dumbbell above your chest with arms extended. Sit up while keeping the weight overhead at arm's length, then lower back down under control.

name: Overhead Chest Stretch
description: A static stretch that opens the chest by extending the arms overhead and pulling back.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, interlace your fingers and extend your arms overhead. Gently pull your arms back and upward, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.

name: Pec Deck Fly
description: A machine-based isolation exercise focusing on squeezing the chest muscles through a fly motion.
instructions: Sit on the pec deck machine with forearms against the pads and elbows slightly bent. Bring the arms together by contracting the chest, then slowly return to the starting position while maintaining control.

name: Peroneals Stretch
description: A static stretch that targets the outside muscles of the lower leg.
instructions: Sit or stand and cross one leg over the other, gently turning the sole of the foot inwards to feel a stretch along the outside of the lower leg. Hold the stretch, then repeat on the other side.

name: Pilates Corkscrew
description: A Pilates core exercise where the legs draw a circular motion to challenge abdominal stability.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms at your sides and legs extended overhead. Lift your hips slightly off the mat, then circle your legs in a controlled motion, using your core to stabilize and reverse the direction after each circle.

name: Pilates Hundred
description: A classic Pilates exercise involving rhythmic arm pumps and core engagement.
instructions: Lie on your back with legs extended or in tabletop position. Lift your head, neck, and shoulders off the mat, extend arms, and pulse them up and down in small, quick movements while holding the core contracted for 100 counts.

name: Plyometric Side Lunge Stretch
description: A dynamic stretch to warm up and mobilize the hips, inner thighs, and legs.
instructions: Begin standing with feet shoulder-width apart. Step to the side into a deep lunge, keeping the opposite leg straight, and quickly alternate sides in a rhythmic motion.

name: Pull-Up
description: A bodyweight pulling exercise that develops lat and upper body strength using a hanging bar.
instructions: Grab a pull-up bar with either a pronated (overhand, pull-up) or supinated (underhand, chin-up) grip slightly wider or narrower than shoulder width as desired. Start from a dead hang, retract your shoulders, and pull your chin above the bar using your back and arms. Control your descent back to the bottom.

name: Pull-Up (Wide Grip)
description: A pull-up variation performed with a wide, overhand grip to emphasize the upper lats and back.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with hands wider than shoulders using an overhand grip. Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar, then lower slowly.

name: Push-Up
description: A bodyweight exercise performed in a prone position, targeting the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
instructions: Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Lower your body by bending elbows until your chest nearly touches the floor, then push back to the starting position while keeping your core engaged.

name: Rear Decline Bridge
description: A bodyweight floor bridge that lifts the hips to train the glutes and hamstrings while keeping the shoulders on the ground.
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent. Place your arms by your sides with your palms facing down. Engage your glutes and hamstrings, and lift your hips off the ground until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. Hold this position for a few seconds, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Pushing through the toes so the heels lift
Overarching the lower back at the top
Dropping the hips quickly to the floor

name: Rear Deltoid Stretch
description: A stretch that targets the rear shoulder to enhance flexibility and reduce tension.
instructions: Stand or sit upright, extend one arm across your body at shoulder height and use the opposite hand to pull it closer, feeling a stretch across the back of the shoulder. Hold, then switch sides.

name: Rear Foot Elevated Hip Flexor Stretch
description: A deep hip flexor stretch with the rear foot elevated for improved flexibility.
instructions: Stand facing away from a bench or sturdy platform. Place one foot on the bench behind you and lower into a lunge, feeling a stretch in the hip flexors of the elevated leg. Keep your torso upright and pelvis tucked for maximum benefit.

name: Resistance Band High Fly
description: A chest isolation movement where resistance bands are used to fly arms downward from above shoulder height.
instructions: Attach bands above head height and hold one handle in each hand. Stand with arms overhead in a wide position, then pull hands down and together in an arc, squeezing the chest. Return slowly to the start.

name: Reverse Crunch
description: A bodyweight abs exercise lifting the hips toward the chest to target the lower abdominals.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides and knees bent at 90 degrees. Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest, then slowly lower back to the starting position without letting your feet touch the floor.
commonMistakes: Letting lower back arch off the floor

name: Reverse Dip Stretch
description: A stretch targeting the triceps and shoulders by extending the arms behind the body and lowering the torso.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and place your hands behind you with fingers facing forward. Gently press through your palms to lift your chest and feel the stretch across your upper arms and shoulders, holding the position without hyperextending your elbows.

name: Reverse Grip Machine Lat Pulldown
description: A machine pulldown using an underhand grip to train the lats through a vertical pulling motion.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your knees under the pads and your feet flat on the ground. Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Sit upright with your chest out and shoulders back, maintaining a slight arch in your lower back. Pull the handles down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Leaning far back and turning it into a row
Pulling the handles behind the neck
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Letting the weight slam back at the top

name: Reverse Grip Pull-Up
description: A vertical bodyweight pulling exercise with palms facing you, emphasizing the lats and biceps.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width, underhand (supinated) grip. Pull your chin above the bar by flexing your elbows and squeezing your lats, then lower under control.

name: Reverse-Grip Cable Lat Pulldown
description: A cable pulldown variation using an underhand (supinated) grip to emphasize the lower lats and biceps.
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown station and grasp the bar with a reverse (underhand) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Pull the bar down to your upper chest, squeezing the shoulder blades together, then slowly return to starting position.

name: Ring High Row
description: A suspended horizontal pulling movement using rings set high to target upper back and rear shoulder muscles.
instructions: Set up rings at an appropriate height and grip handles with palms facing in. Lean back with body rigid, arms extended, and feet forward. Pull your chest up to ring height, squeezing the shoulder blades together, then lower back under control.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: A hip hinge with a barbell that loads the hamstrings and glutes through a long stretch.
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar at your hips. With a slight bend in the knees, push your hips back and slide the bar down your thighs until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand.
commonMistakes: Lowering further than the hamstrings allow

name: Rotational Push-Up
description: A push-up variation involving a torso rotation to challenge the chest, shoulders, triceps, and core.
instructions: From a push-up position, lower down as normal. As you press up, rotate your torso and extend one arm toward the ceiling, forming a T with your arms. Return to push-up position and repeat to the other side.

name: Runner's Stretch
description: A flexibility exercise targeting the hip flexors and hamstrings by stepping one leg forward into a deep lunge.
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with one foot forward and the other leg extended back, keeping both hands on the floor. Sink your hips low toward the ground while keeping your chest lifted, feeling a stretch in the hip flexor of your rear leg and hamstring of your front leg.

name: Running
description: A repetitive aerobic movement that improves cardiovascular fitness and endurance.
instructions: Begin at a comfortable pace, maintaining upright posture and relaxed shoulders. Land lightly on your feet and use a natural arm swing for balance, adjusting speed and distance as fitness improves.

name: Russian Twist on Stability Ball (Arms Straight)
description: An advanced core exercise targeting the obliques by rotating the torso while balanced on a stability ball with arms extended.
instructions: Sit on a stability ball with feet flat on the ground, then walk feet forward to roll down until your upper back is supported. Extend your arms straight in front and rotate your torso side to side, keeping arms aligned and abs engaged throughout.
aliases: Russian Twist (on stability ball arms straight)

name: Scapula Dips
description: A bodyweight shoulder-blade dip on straight arms that trains scapular control and shoulder depression in a supported position.
instructions: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended in front of you. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight. Lower your body by bending your elbows and retracting your shoulder blades, as if you are trying to squeeze a pencil between them. Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your hands to extend your elbows and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows like a regular dip
Swinging the legs or torso to create momentum
Shrugging up and never pressing back down
Dropping too far and losing shoulder control

name: Seated Alternating Dumbbell Curl
description: A seated exercise curling dumbbells alternately to build bicep size and strength.
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Curl one dumbbell by flexing the elbow, then lower it and repeat with the opposite arm, keeping your torso stable.

name: Seated Bent Over Back Stretch
description: A static stretch performed while seated, bending forward to lengthen the lower and upper back muscles.
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended or crossed. Hinge at the hips and slowly bend forward, reaching hands toward feet or out in front, keeping the back as relaxed as comfortable. Hold the stretch to gently lengthen the muscles along the spine.

name: Seated Boat Stretch
description: A seated flexibility stretch focusing on the inner thighs and hips.
instructions: Sit on the floor and bring the soles of your feet together, letting knees fall out to the sides. Hold your feet or ankles and gently pull them in, leaning forward slightly to deepen the stretch through the groin and hips.
formCues: Go only as far as comfortable

name: Seated Cable Row (V-Grip)
description: A compound cable exercise targeting the mid-back and lats using a V-grip handle.
instructions: Sit on a cable row station with feet on the platform and grasp the V-grip handle. Keep your back straight and pull the handle towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows. Control the return to the starting position.
aliases: cable reverse-grip straight back seated high row

name: Seated Cable Row (Wide-Grip)
description: A cable row variation using a wide grip to target the upper back and rear deltoids.
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with feet on the platform and grab the wide grip handle. Pull the bar towards the upper abdomen, retracting the shoulder blades, and return to the starting position with control.

name: Seated Calf Stretch
description: A stretch performed while seated, focusing on lengthening the calf muscles.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended. Loop a towel or band around the ball of one foot, keeping your knee straight, and gently pull your toes toward you, feeling a stretch in the calf. Hold and repeat on the other side.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: A pressing movement targeting the shoulders, performed seated with dumbbells.
instructions: Sit upright with back supported and hold dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing forward. Press the weights up overhead until arms are extended, then lower back down under control.

name: Seated Lower Back Stretch
description: A gentle forward reaching stretch to relieve tension in the lower back while seated.
instructions: Sit on the floor or chair with your legs extended or crossed. Reach both arms forward and slowly bend at the hips, lowering your torso and arms toward your feet, feeling the stretch across your lower back. Hold the position, keeping the back relaxed.

name: Seated Shoulder Flexor, Depressor, Retractor Stretch
description: A seated stretch focusing on improving flexibility and mobility in the front, lower, and rear shoulder muscles.
instructions: Sit upright on the floor or a chair with feet flat. Reach one or both arms overhead, then gently pull the shoulders downward and backward to open the chest and lengthen the front and rear deltoids. Maintain a tall posture and breathe deeply.
aliases: Stretching - Seated Shoulder Flexor Depresor Retractor
roller seated shoulder flexor depressor retractor

name: Seated Straight Arm Twist
description: Seated torso rotation with arms straight to target the obliques and core stability.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet elevated or flat. Extend both arms straight out in front of you, clasping your hands together. Rotate your torso to one side, keeping arms straight, then rotate to the other side while engaging your core throughout.
commonMistakes: Using just arms instead of rotating the torso
Moving too quickly or without control

name: Seated Twist on Stability Ball
description: A rotational core exercise performed while seated on a stability ball to target the obliques.
instructions: Sit upright on a stability ball, feet flat and hip-width apart. Twist your torso to one side while keeping hips steady, then return to center and repeat on the other side.

name: Seated Twist Stretch (Straight Arm)
description: A flexibility exercise involving seated trunk rotation to stretch the obliques and lower back.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and back straight. Extend your right arm behind you and twist your torso to the right, keeping your left arm straight across your knee for leverage, hold, and repeat on the other side.

name: Seated Wide Angle Pose Sequence
description: A sequence of stretches performed in a wide-legged seated position to improve hip, hamstring, and lower back flexibility.
instructions: Sit upright and spread your legs as wide as is comfortable. With a straight back, hinge forward at the hips and walk your hands out in front or toward each leg, deepening the stretch in the inner thighs and lower back. Carefully progress through variations to target various muscle groups.
aliases: Stretching - Seated Wide Angle Pose Sequence

name: Shoulder-Width Pull-Up
description: A classic bodyweight exercise targeting the lats and upper back with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width apart, palms facing away. Initiate movement from the back and pull your chin over the bar, then lower yourself in a controlled manner back to the starting position.

name: Side Bend on Stability Ball
description: A lateral flexion movement performed on a stability ball to target the obliques.
instructions: Lie sideways over a stability ball, feet anchored, and hands behind head. Crunch your torso upward in a side-bending motion, then lower with control.

name: Side Bend Stretch
description: A standing lateral bending stretch focusing on lengthening the obliques and side body muscles.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart or sit upright. Raise one arm overhead and lean to the opposite side, feeling a stretch along your side and back muscles. Hold briefly, then return to start and repeat on the other side.

name: Side Plank
description: A core-strengthening hold performed on one side, engaging the obliques and stabilizing hip muscles.
instructions: Lie on one side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs extended. Lift your hips off the ground to form a straight line from head to feet, bracing your abs and holding the position while breathing steadily.

name: Side Wrist Pull Stretch
description: A standing or seated stretch for the wrist and forearm, involving lateral arm extension and gentle pulling.
instructions: Stand or sit upright, extend one arm overhead or to the side, and grasp the wrist with your opposite hand. Gently pull the wrist to the side to stretch the forearm and wrist muscles, avoiding excessive force.

name: Single Dumbbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
description: A stiff-legged deadlift variation using a single dumbbell to target the hamstrings and lower back.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell with both hands in front of your thighs. With a slight bend at the knees, hinge at the hips to lower the dumbbell until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings and then return to the starting position.

name: Single Leg Stretch (Bent Knee)
description: A floor stretch to target hip flexors and hamstrings by pulling one bent leg towards the chest.
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent. Grip one shin and gently pull that knee towards your chest, feeling the stretch in your hip and glutes. Maintain a neutral spine and hold before switching legs.

name: Single Straight Leg Stretch
description: A floor stretch focusing on the hamstrings by raising and holding one straight leg toward the body.
instructions: Lie on your back, legs extended. Lift one leg straight up, keeping it as straight as possible, and hold the calf or thigh to gently pull it closer, feeling a stretch in the hamstrings and calves. Then switch legs.
formCues: Point or flex foot for deeper stretch

name: Sit-Up
description: A classic ab exercise involving lifting the torso from the floor to a seated position to build core strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the ground. Place your hands behind your head or across your chest, engage your core, and lift your torso all the way up to your knees, then lower back down with control.

name: Sled 45 Degree Calf Press
description: A seated calf exercise on a 45-degree sled where you press through the balls of your feet to raise and lower the heels.
instructions: Adjust the sled machine to a 45-degree angle. Place your feet on the sled platform with your toes pointing forward. Push the sled platform away from you by extending your ankles and calves. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the sled platform back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Drive through the balls of feet
Lift heels as high as possible
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the knees instead of moving only at the ankles
Placing the whole foot flat on the platform so the heels cannot drop
Bouncing out of the bottom instead of lowering under control
Turning the toes excessively in or out during the rep

name: Sled 45 Degree Wide Leg Press
description: A compound lower body movement targeting the quadriceps with emphasis on glutes and adductors due to a wide foot stance.
instructions: Sit on a 45-degree leg press machine with feet placed wider than hip-width on the platform. Push the platform up to release the safety handles and slowly lower it toward your chest, then drive through your heels to press the weight back up.
formCues: Keep knees in line with toes
Do not lock knees at top

name: Sled Hack Squat
